passage.title: The Strange World of Sight
paragraphs: Seeing is believing, it is said. But could it be the other way round?

Two of the great British men of the 17th century, the philosopher John Locke and the physicist Isaac Newton, were both aware that objects are not coloured, and that against all appearances light is not coloured either. This is still not generally recognised even now, 400 years later, because it seems so implausible. Yet it tells us something very important — that perceptions are not identical with what we perceive, and may be very different.

The most accurate historical account of perception is that of the 19th-century German scientist Hermann von Helmholtz. However, it was ridiculed at the time. Von Helmholtz thought that perceptions are unconscious inferences we make based on a combination of clues provided by the eyes and other senses, and knowledge of the world. This idea of unconscious inference for perception preceded, by several years, the psychoanalyst Freud's notion of the unconscious, which was also initially treated with derision because it undermined the notion of humans as pre-eminently rational beings who could be held responsible for their actions and awarded blame or praise accordingly.

Crucially, perception of the present depends on rich, though of course not always correct or appropriate, knowledge from the past. We interpret sense data (what we hear, touch, taste, see and smell) from the present according to what we already know. This raises the question: if we see the present through memory, why aren't past and present confused?

The pioneering Russian neurologist Alexander Luria described the case of Mr S, who had a remarkable memory; however, he was prone to just such confusions, for example mistaking seeing his clock for remembering it, and so failing to get up in the morning. This suggests that perhaps an important function of perception is to underline the present. Individual perceptions have a vividness that is rare for memories, which might be how we are able to separate them. Try this: look at something for a few seconds, and then shut your eyes and visualise it in memory. You will almost certainly find that the memory is pale by comparison with the perception. Perhaps this is why past and present are not normally confused. Luria's Mr S had exceptionally vivid memories, and rich synaesthesia — experiencing perceptions from another sense as well as the one being stimulated, such as musical notes experienced as colours — which may be why he confused seeing with having seen.

The complexity of processes involved in how we see first impressed itself on me 45 years ago. With my colleague Jean Wallace, I studied the rare case of Sydney Bradford, a man who had been born blind but, through a corneal graft at the age of 52, suddenly found himself able to see. Although immediately after the operation he was able to 'see', he could only see those things that he already knew about, having experienced them through touch. It was his touch memories that enabled him to perceive them with his eyes. When Bradford was first taken to the zoo, he proved utterly unable to see an elephant as he had no knowledge to make sense of his perceptions.

The more recent case in California of Mike May, who was also born blind, is similar. Since his operation, his sight has gradually improved as he learns to see, for example, by understanding how shadows represent depth and tell us about the shape of things. Some of the consequences of May's new-found vision were less happy. He had been a champion blind skier, but following the operation, he would have to shut his eyes while skiing to block out what he now found was a terrifying sight.

But acceptance of this intimate connection between memory and perception, even though it was first noticed in the 17th century, has been slow in brain science. Despite the fact that state-of-the-art brain imaging shows that perception animates parts of the brain associated with both present information and memory, most research on memory and perception is still undertaken as if these were separate processes. Seeing used to be thought of as taking place only in the eyes, and in quite specialised brain regions; but now it seems that half the brain is occupied with seeing, requiring a lot of energy. Perhaps this is why we shut our eyes for a rest.

It is not just extreme cases like Mike May, but also much more common errors of seeing — illusions — that can reveal the crucial role of memory in governing what we (think we) see. Perception depends on specific knowledge and probabilities. Our brains calculate the likelihood of what is out there, and when too far-fetched, perceptions are rejected.

A dramatic and discomforting example is looking at the two sides of a face-mask. From the front it is a convex shape with the nose sticking out. Then if the mask is rotated, the back of the mask will be seen as convex, though we know that it must be concave. It is almost, if not quite, impossible to sketch the back of a hollow mask to look as it is — hollow. Science often learns from what does not happen: people not seeing a hollow face as hollow is the most revealing experiment on perception. The unsettling truth from brain science is that even people with no visual impairment see what, at some level, they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are.

question_groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C, or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 27–30 on your answer sheet.

questions.text: Why does the writer refer to Locke and Newton in the first paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: to indicate that his article will cover several scientific fields

options.label: B
options.text: to stress how much physics has changed in 400 years

options.label: C
options.text: to persuade the reader to take him seriously

options.label: D
options.text: to point out that his notions are not new

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Tại sao tác giả đề cập đến Locke và Newton trong đoạn đầu tiên?

Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Hai trong số những người Anh vĩ đại của thế kỷ 17, triết gia John Locke và nhà vật lý Isaac Newton, đều nhận thức được rằng các vật thể không có màu sắc... Điều này vẫn chưa được công nhận rộng rãi cho đến nay, 400 năm sau".
==> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu D (to point out that his notions are not new — để chỉ ra rằng những quan niệm này không phải là mới).

Bước 3: Đáp án: D

Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án A -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến việc "bài viết sẽ đề cập đến nhiều lĩnh vực khoa học".
Đáp án B -> Đoạn văn không đề cập đến việc "vật lý học đã thay đổi bao nhiêu trong 400 năm".
Đáp án C -> Đoạn văn không nói về việc "thuyết phục người đọc tin tưởng tác giả".
quotes: Two of the great British men of the 17th century, the philosopher John Locke and the physicist Isaac Newton, were both aware that objects are not coloured, and that against all appearances light is not coloured either. This is still not generally recognised even now, 400 years later, because it seems so implausible.

questions.text: According to the writer, why was Freud's theory of the unconscious mocked?

options.label: A
options.text: It was too complex for his contemporaries to understand.

options.label: B
options.text: It involved criticism of the way people behaved in society.

options.label: C
options.text: People felt that it devalued the accepted concept of humanity.

options.label: D
options.text: People assumed that it was intended as a joke.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Theo tác giả, tại sao lý thuyết về vô thức của Freud bị chế nhạo?

Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Thuyết vô thức của Freud cũng ban đầu bị coi thường vì nó làm suy yếu quan niệm về con người là những sinh vật lý trí tối cao, những người có thể bị quy trách nhiệm cho hành động của họ".
==> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu C (People felt that it devalued the accepted concept of humanity — Mọi người cảm thấy nó làm giảm giá trị quan niệm được chấp nhận về nhân loại).

Bước 3: Đáp án: C

Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án A -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến việc "lý thuyết quá phức tạp để những người cùng thời hiểu".
Đáp án B -> Đoạn văn không đề cập đến việc "chỉ trích cách mọi người hành xử trong xã hội".
Đáp án D -> Đoạn văn không nói về việc "mọi người cho rằng đó là một trò đùa"
quotes: This idea of unconscious inference for perception preceded, by several years, the psychoanalyst Freud's notion of the unconscious, which was also initially treated with derision because it undermined the notion of humans as pre-eminently rational beings who could be held responsible for their actions and awarded blame or praise accordingly.

options.label: A
options.text: how valuable knowledge of the past can be.

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

quotes: The pioneering Russian neurologist Alexander Luria described the case of Mr S, who had a remarkable memory; however, he was prone to just such confusions, for example mistaking seeing his clock for remembering it, and so failing to get up in the morning. This suggests that perhaps an important function of perception is to underline the present. Individual perceptions have a vividness that is rare for memories, which might be how we are able to separate them.

questions.text: What point is the writer making in the text as a whole?

options.label: A
options.text: Perception involves much more than the data collected by the eyes.

options.label: B
options.text: Learning to see as an adult can be a time-consuming process.

options.label: C
options.text: Science is failing to devote enough attention to sight.

options.label: D
options.text: Human perception is remarkably reliable.

quotes: Crucially, perception of the present depends on rich, though of course not always correct or appropriate, knowledge from the past. We interpret sense data (what we hear, touch, taste, see and smell) from the present according to what we already know.

question_groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage?

questions.text: Sydney Bradford relied on recollections of objects he had touched to help him see after his operation.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Sydney Bradford dựa vào ký ức xúc giác về các vật thể để giúp ông nhìn thấy sau ca phẫu thuật.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
touch memories ~ recollections of objects he had touched
perceive with his eyes ~ see after his operation
Bradford ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Chính những ký ức xúc giác của Bradford đã cho phép ông nhận thức được chúng bằng mắt".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Bradford dựa vào ký ức xúc giác để nhìn sau phẫu thuật" (It was his touch memories that enabled him to perceive them with his eyes).

Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: Although immediately after the operation he was able to 'see', he could only see those things that he already knew about, having experienced them through touch. It was his touch memories that enabled him to perceive them with his eyes.

questions.text: People who only start to see as adults can learn to see as other people do in time.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những người chỉ bắt đầu nhìn thấy khi đã trưởng thành có thể học cách nhìn như người khác theo thời gian.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
sight has gradually improved ~ learn to see in time
Mike May ~ people who only start to see as adults
learns to see ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Kể từ ca phẫu thuật, thị lực của ông dần dần được cải thiện khi ông học cách nhìn, ví dụ như hiểu cách bóng đổ thể hiện chiều sâu".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "có thể học cách nhìn theo thời gian" (his sight has gradually improved as he learns to see).

Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: Since his operation, his sight has gradually improved as he learns to see, for example, by understanding how shadows represent depth and tell us about the shape of things.

questions.text: People who have gained their sight as adults find certain activities harder to do than before.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những người có được thị lực khi đã trưởng thành thấy một số hoạt động khó thực hiện hơn so với trước đây.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
shut his eyes while skiing ~ certain activities harder to do
terrifying sight ~ harder than before
Mike May ~ people who have gained sight as adults

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Ông từng là một vận động viên trượt tuyết mù vô địch, nhưng sau ca phẫu thuật, ông phải nhắm mắt lại khi trượt tuyết để ngăn chặn những gì ông thấy là một cảnh tượng đáng sợ".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "một số hoạt động trở nên khó khăn hơn sau khi có thị lực" (he would have to shut his eyes while skiing to block out what he now found was a terrifying sight).

Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: Some of the consequences of May's new-found vision were less happy. He had been a champion blind skier, but following the operation, he would have to shut his eyes while skiing to block out what he now found was a terrifying sight.

questions.text: It is evident now that sight involves the eyes and one particular area of the brain.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Hiện nay rõ ràng rằng thị giác liên quan đến mắt và một vùng não cụ thể.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
half the brain ~ one particular area of the brain
seeing ~ sight
specialised brain regions ~ one particular area

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Việc nhìn trước đây được cho là chỉ xảy ra ở mắt và các vùng não chuyên biệt; nhưng bây giờ có vẻ như một nửa não bộ bận rộn với việc nhìn".
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "chỉ một vùng não cụ thể" (now it seems that half the brain is occupied with seeing).

Bước 4: Đáp án: NO
quotes: Seeing used to be thought of as taking place only in the eyes, and in quite specialised brain regions; but now it seems that half the brain is occupied with seeing, requiring a lot of energy.

questions.text: The mask experiment is particularly useful in training people who are regaining their sight.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Thí nghiệm mặt nạ đặc biệt hữu ích trong việc huấn luyện những người đang lấy lại thị lực.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
mask experiment ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
training people ~ không tìm thấy tương đương
regaining their sight ~ không tìm thấy tương đương

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến thí nghiệm mặt nạ như một ví dụ về vai trò của ký ức trong tri giác.
==> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin "thí nghiệm mặt nạ được dùng để huấn luyện người lấy lại thị lực" (The mask experiment is particularly useful in training people who are regaining their sight).

Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN
quotes: A dramatic and discomforting example is looking at the two sides of a face-mask. From the front it is a convex shape with the nose sticking out. Then if the mask is rotated, the back of the mask will be seen as convex, though we know that it must be concave. It is almost, if not quite, impossible to sketch the back of a hollow mask to look as it is — hollow. Science often learns from what does not happen: people not seeing a hollow face as hollow is the most revealing experiment on perception.

questions.text: People with perfect vision can fail to interpret objects correctly under certain circumstances.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những người có thị lực hoàn hảo vẫn có thể không diễn giải đúng các vật thể trong một số hoàn cảnh nhất định.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
no visual impairment ~ perfect vision
see what they expect to see ~ fail to interpret objects correctly
miss things as they really are ~ under certain circumstances

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Sự thật đáng lo ngại từ khoa học thần kinh là ngay cả những người không có khiếm khuyết thị giác cũng nhìn thấy những gì họ kỳ vọng thấy, và thường bỏ lỡ những thứ như chúng thực sự là".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "người có thị lực hoàn hảo vẫn có thể không diễn giải đúng vật thể" (even people with no visual impairment see what they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are).

Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: The unsettling truth from brain science is that even people with no visual impairment see what, at some level, they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are.

question_groups.body:
The mask experiment
In this experiment, having looked at the front of a simple face-mask, subjects look at the reverse. However, the subjects are convinced that they are still looking at a mask which is ____ (37) in shape. They believe that the ____ (38) is poking out in the normal manner because that is what they are used to seeing. Attempting to make a ____ (39) of the mask in this orientation leads to the same problem. The subjects fail to see a concave form because of the ____ (40) they have that features of a face stick out.
